top_signals.title: Nvidia Pares Gains on Blackwell Report; Altria Lower | Stock Movers
top_signals.summary:
Today's biggest winners and losers in the stock market.

On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Nvidia (NVDA) shares are higher even though news broke this morning that a pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp's powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia's most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators.

- Altria (MO) shares are declining after the company issued a statement on Nov. 26 confirming early media speculation that it is considering an all cash offer for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands. 

- SAP (SAP) shares are moving in response to news it is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Iraq Delays Up to 30 Million Barrels of Crude Oil Shipments
top_signals.summary: Iraq’s SOMO has delayed loadings of crude oil cargoes to the tune of between 20 and 30 million barrels, according to a Bloomberg report citing unnamed sources. The reason for the delays has not been established yet, but the cargoes were supposed to be loaded this month; now, only some of them will be loaded, and only during the first ten days of December, the report said. top_signals.title: U.S. Encouraged Iraq and Venezuela to Leave OPEC, Sources Say
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Administration early this year encouraged two of OPEC’s five founding members, Iraq and Venezuela, to leave the cartel, Reuters reported on Friday, quoting multiple sources with knowledge of the matter. Iraq and Venezuela have brushed aside this push from the Trump Administration, so far. The U.S. Administration wanted oil production in both Iraq and Venezuela to increase, and was concerned that the OPEC and OPEC+ agreements and production quotas would hamstring any output gains. top_signals.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
top_signals.summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

top_signals.title: Almost 60% of primary energy used for electricity is lost to conversion and transmission
top_signals.summary: In 2025, the United States consumed 34 quadrillion British thermal units (quads) of primary energy to deliver 14 quads of electricity sales to end users, with nearly 60% lost. About 95% of the losses came from converting primary energy into electricity, mostly due to lost heat from burning coal and natural gas. The remaining 5% was lost in the course of delivering electricity across grid infrastructure to homes and businesses.
